title: Silas and the Provision
premise: Wren Kavanagh, a mountain guide blacklisted from Nepal and Peru and drowning in debt to a ruthless outfitter, is guiding one last illegal trek when a dying prospector named Silas trades a map to a river-hidden inheritance for a promise: deliver it to a daughter Silas abandoned decades ago. Pursued by the outfitter's enforcers who want the map, Wren descends into monsoon country with a leaking boat and an unexpected ally, Mara, a river pilot with her own reasons to vanish. As the storm closes in, Wren learns the inheritance is not gold but land deeds—and that Silas's daughter is Mara herself. In the climax, Wren must choose between selling the map to clear their debt or delivering it whole; they choose the promise, outlast the flood, and finally stop running, finding belonging not in a place but in keeping faith.
about_author: Rafael Almeida is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons on monsoon waterways before turning to writing full-time. They live between two port towns and write about people who can't go home.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Blacklisted and broke, Wren takes an off-the-books trek through border mountains, establishing their skill, cynicism, and crushing debt to outfitter Dario Voss. Emotional beat: weary self-containment—the belief that invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Last Camp
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The trek stumbles on a dying prospector, Silas, stranded above the treeline. He offers Wren a weathered map and a sealed letter in exchange for one promise: find his daughter. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion cracking Wren's armor.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Silas dies at dawn; Wren buries him and pockets the map, telling themselves it's just payment. But Voss's scouts appear on the ridge, asking questions. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss learns of Silas's map—rumored deeds to river gold claims—and sends enforcers after Wren, revealing how much leverage he holds over Wren's past. Emotional beat: cold menace; the noose tightening.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fleeing overland, Wren reaches a river town and buys a leaking boat with borrowed money. First glimpse of Mara, a pilot who refuses all passengers. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Says No
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara watches the stranger with the haunted eyes and the old map sketch, recognizing the river route her father once described. She refuses to help—but can't sleep after. Emotional beat: buried grief stirring.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Voss's enforcers corner Wren; Mara intervenes with a boat hook and a hard bargain: she'll run the river if Wren never asks about her past. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged under threat.

chapters.title: Leaking Hull, Rising Water
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They launch ahead of the monsoon front; the boat takes on water and tempers fray as Mara questions what's really on the map. Emotional beat: friction masking mutual respect.

chapters.title: The First Rapid
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A night run through rapids nearly kills them; Wren's quick thinking saves the cargo—and Mara notices. Emotional beat: trust earned in white water.

chapters.title: What Silas Carried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Examining the map's margins, Wren finds sketches of a young girl and realizes Silas tracked his daughter's life from afar for years. Emotional beat: tenderness toward a stranger; doubt about the promise's cost.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Shared POV. A bribed river official tips off Voss's men; Wren and Mara bluff through a checkpoint, but Wren's face is recognized. Emotional beat: fear that the past has caught up.

chapters.title: Monsoon Country
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Rain sets in for days; marooned in a flooded side channel, the two trade stories by lamplight—almost everything but the truth each guards. Emotional beat: intimacy growing in forced stillness.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren secretly reads Silas's letter and learns the daughter's name: Mara Vane. Shocked, Wren hides it, torn between honesty and fear of losing her. Emotional beat: the first true moral weight of the promise.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Voss's enforcers catch up and slash the hull; the boat sinks in a backwater. They lose supplies and half the map drowns—though Wren memorized it. Emotional beat: rage, then grim adaptation.

chapters.title: Walking the Flooded Forest
chapters.summary: Shared POV. On foot through drowned jungle, they reach a village where Mara is known—and where an elder reveals that Silas came looking for her years ago and was turned away. Emotional beat: Mara's world tilting.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Voss himself arrives, offering to erase Wren's debt in exchange for the map and deeds. Wren stalls, discovering the deeds are worthless as gold but vital to villagers' land claims—including land Mara's father meant for her. Emotional beat: temptation met with clarity.

chapters.title: Confession in the Rain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Wren tells Mara the truth: the map was her father's, the letter hers, the promise his dying wish. Mara's fury gives way to reading the letter alone in the rain. Emotional beat: heartbreak opening into something like forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Shared POV. With Voss closing in, they steal his own patrol boat and make a final run upriver to the land Silas deeded, racing the crest of the flood. Emotional beat: all-in courage; no retreat left.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax: Voss corners them at the deed house as the river breaches its banks. Wren publicly surrenders the map—not to Voss, but to the village council, voiding Voss's claim and ending Wren's debt by exposing his fraud. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: After the River
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Flood recedes; Voss flees downstream ahead of the authorities. Mara stands on her father's land, grieving and unburdened, and asks Wren to stay—not out of debt, but choice. Emotional beat: belonging offered freely.

chapters.title: The Compass Point North
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren sells the compass that symbolized the running life and buys stakes in Mara's ferry run, sending word to clear their name legally. Emotional beat: quiet transformation—from invisible to rooted.

chapters.title: Silas and the Provision
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue. One year later, the ferry carries pilgrims and farmers; a stone marks Silas's grave overlooking the water. Wren guides travelers again—this time with papers, a partner, and a home. Emotional beat: peace earned; the promise kept.
